Q: Should I focus on coding exercises or building projects to learn C++? A:

Exactly. There is no substitute for "butt in chair" time working through a peer-reviewed book from The Definitive C++ Book Guide and List, and doing the examples in the book. Add to that the cppreference.com site as your reference site so you can further learn the details of how each of the classes and features of the language work and you have the information needed to learn.

Coding challenge sites (hackerank, etc.) and sites like CS50 are not teaching sites, they are sites that provide problems to solve based on what you have learned elsewhere. The challenges are good practice, but they do not teach you C++. You will get more out of them with that understanding.

Be very wary of other online "learn C++ here" sites. Some are woefully outdated, and some are just plain wrong, providing tutorials on how C++ was written at the time of the first C standard. The books from the list, cpprefence.com, and the C++ Language Standard as you progress should be your primary sources. Good luck with your coding.

Q: Key counter in C, how to pause and resume for key logging A:

Wouldn't you want to identify the F1 keycode in your KeyboardProc function and toggle a flag indicating whether the collection of the count was paused or not by setting/unsetting the flag? If currently counting and F1 pressed, then set the, e.g. pausecount flag true and you could condition your count on if (pausecount != true) { counter++; } or something similar.

Q: Only one --hash-style in embedded Linux. Why? A:

The dynamic linker can and does figure out the kind of hash table ("sysv" or "gnu") present in the ELF and works accordingly.

Unfortunately what you see is a case where support for gnu hash sections has NOT been back-ported to older version of the dynamic linker in use on your system.

A similar situation exists wherein binaries built for RHEL5/FC6 do NOT work on RHEL4/FC5.

Why .gnu.hash is incompatible with .hash(sysv)?

Generating an ELF with the gnu hash section imposes certain restrictions(additional rules) on the construction of the dynamic symbol table.

With GNU hash, the dynamic symbol table is divided into two parts. The first part receives the symbols that can be omitted from the hash table. GNU hash does not impose any specific order for the symbols in this part of the dynamic symbol table.

The second part of the dynamic symbol table receives the symbols that are accessible from the hash table. These symbols are required to be sorted by increasing (hash % nbuckets) value, using the GNU hash function described above. The number of hash buckets (nbuckets) is recorded in the GNU hash section, described below. As a result, symbols which will be found in a single hash chain are adjacent in memory, leading to better cache performance.

Reference: blogs.oracle.com/ali/entry/gnu_hash_elf_sections

Q: Cannot import "visual" in vpython due to NumPy import error A:

The problem is not with the Python installation but with the numpy module.

From the command line type:

pip install numpy --upgrade

This command will either install the numpy module if you don't have it, or it will upgrade it to the 64-bit version.

If you have never used pip then navigate to C:/Python27/Lib/site-packages/pip/, double click on the init.py file and then double click on the main.py file. This will install pip which you can then use to download any Python module from the command line by typing:

pip install "module name"
